title: Tangent space of a product is a direct sum
statement: Let k be a field, let X and Y be k-schemes, and let x in X and y in Y be k-rational points ($\kappa(x)=\kappa(y)=k$) [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Then the map induced by the two projections is a k-linear isomorphism T_{X \times_k Y/k,(x,y)} \cong T_{X/k,x} \oplus T_{Y/k,y}. Its inverse sends (v,0) to d(1,y)(v) and (0,w) to d(x,1)(w), where (1,y): X \to X \times_k Y and (x,1): Y \to X \times_k Y are the maps built from the structure maps and the k-rational points y and x.

proof.text: Let p_X and p_Y be the two projections. Composition with them sends a tangent vector at (x,y) to tangent vectors at x and y, and the residue fields are k in all three cases. By [lem-sc-tangent-map-linear] these maps are k-linear, so they define a k-linear map Phi from T_{X x_k Y/k,(x,y)} to T_{X/k,x} direct-sum T_{Y/k,y}.

source.place: Tag 0BEB, statement and proof: map induced by the two projections

proof.text: Let i_X=(1,y):X \to X \times_k Y and i_Y=(x,1):Y \to X \times_k Y. For (v,w) define Psi(v,w)=d i_X(v)+d i_Y(w), using the vector-space structure of [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space]. The composites p_X i_X and p_Y i_Y are identities, while p_Y i_X and p_X i_Y are the constant maps at y and x. A constant map sends every tangent vector to the zero vector because its composite with a dual-number point factors through Spec k, so [lem-sc-tangent-map-linear] and the zero element described in [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space] give Phi(Psi(v,w))=(v,w).

source.place: Tag 0BEB, compatibility with the maps 1 x y and x x 1

proof.text: For a tangent vector theta at (x,y), write (v,w)=Phi(theta), so v=p_X theta and w=p_Y theta. By Step 2, Phi(Psi(v,w))=(v,w), i.e. the morphism Psi(v,w):Spec k[epsilon] \to X \times_k Y has projections p_X Psi(v,w)=v and p_Y Psi(v,w)=w, the same as theta. Both are morphisms of k-schemes Spec k[epsilon] \to X \times_k Y, and v, w are k-morphisms, so by the uniqueness clause of the universal property of the fibre product over Spec k [def-pc-fibre-product] a morphism to X \times_k Y is determined by its two projections; hence Psi(Phi(theta))=theta. So the k-linear map Phi of Step 1 is bijective with inverse Psi, hence a k-linear isomorphism, and Psi(v,0)=d i_X(v)+d i_Y(0)=d i_X(v), Psi(0,w)=d i_Y(w) because d i_Y and d i_X are linear [lem-sc-tangent-map-linear] and so send 0 to the zero vector of [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space].
